clue.text: Opposition from Royal Engineers is over policy

parts.note: RE is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the word policy is laid over the little word is, covering it so it ends up inside

parts.note: a stance is a declared position or policy

explanation.surface: An army engineering corps opposes a proposed policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the container signal here: the policy word is laid over the little word, covering it. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance and opposition are synonyms for pushing back against something.

clue.text: Right behind basic river vessel

parts.note: aft means at or towards the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone stands to the right of and behind a simple boat on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a simple flat floating platform, the most rudimentary craft for a river.

clue.text: Without question, sir lures wild animals

indicators.note: in its old sense 'without' means outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the abbreviation
wild suggests letters running out of control, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man, with no questions asked, tempts wild creatures with bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense it means outside, so the jumble from 'wild' surrounds the question letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Squirrels are small bushy-tailed rodents, an example of animals.

clue.text: Animal the woman kept trimmed at both ends

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: trimming both ends of the word kept leaves just its inner letters

explanation.surface: A woman keeps an animal whose coat is clipped at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed at both ends' strips K and T from KEPT, leaving EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep is a woolly farm animal, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Pull at vehicle, lifting bottom of boot

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word is read upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone tugs at a vehicle stuck by the heel of a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns CART upwards into TRAC; 'bottom of boot' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, the same as to pull it.

clue.text: Traditional girl supporting Conservative in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman backs a Tory who is running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic describes something of lasting, time-honoured style, close to traditional.

clue.text: Wedge lobbed over bunker

indicators.note: a ball lobbed over is flipped end to end, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a wedge of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: A golfer chips a wedge shot over a sand bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf words mislead: 'Wedge' is not the club but a part, and 'lobbed over' turns PART round.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a bunker is a sand trap, so the two words name the same hazard.

clue.text: Luxury car goes for a spin

definitions.meaning: a ... is short for a ...-Royce, the famous luxury car
to turn over and over, as a ball or a plane does

explanation.surface: A posh motor is taken out for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls is both the short name of the Rolls-Royce marque and the verb for turning over repeatedly.

clue.text: Salesman turns up with money! Time for a share

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a cent is a small coin
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sales rep shows up with cash, wanting his cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion or cut of a whole, so it is a share.

clue.text: Loud stringed instrument — or one in the woodwind section

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction for loud
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An orchestral question: a noisy string player, or a member of the woodwinds?
explanation.definitionFit: The flute is a member of the woodwind family in an orchestra.

clue.text: Alert lover abroad to get rid of old tourist

indicators.note: abroad here means widely scattered, so these letters are rearranged once the old letter has gone

explanation.surface: A watchful lover overseas wants to ditch an old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix ALERT LOVER ('abroad') and take out the O ('get rid of old').
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone on a journey, so a tourist is one kind.

clue.text: Dead cross, being held by French and in court

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: et is French for and
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A dead man's cross is carried in a French court.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct describes something no longer living, like a species that has died out.

clue.text: Parrots are pets up in the air

indicators.note: things up in the air are unsettled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Talking birds are pets that fly around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' looks like a noun but is the verb: to parrot is to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words mindlessly, which is what one who repeats does.

clue.text: Discrimination son's shown in gallery

indicators.note: being shown in a place means being put inside it

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy's art is exhibited in a gallery, showing his good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste, in the sense of fine judgement in aesthetic matters, is discrimination.

clue.text: Shows sign of hesitation over gifts

indicators.note: over signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates before opening their presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal, a usage that looks like a positional word in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or show it.

clue.text: Polished table leg — antique, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An antique table leg has been polished, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means refined and graceful, which is what polished describes.

clue.text: Group called in time to make a comeback

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
making a comeback is coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period of time
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A band phoned in, hoping to stage a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' looks like a noun, a band, but it is the verb. 'to make a comeback' turns the time word back to ARE before the call word goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To group things is to arrange or sort them, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: New place to film rears in bed creating clash

indicators.note: in puts one part inside another

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: rearing up turns a word back on itself, so it is reversed

parts.note: a set is where scenes are filmed

explanation.surface: A new film location has actors' backsides in bed, causing a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rears' is a verb, rearing back, so the film-place word turns round; 'in' then puts New plus that inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a struggle or competition, so it is a clash.

clue.text: Tweet quite out of order — women ignored acceptable behaviour

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled, rearranged here after the women letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A rude tweet that ignores women is out of order, not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TWEET QUITE ('out of order') and leave out W ('women ignored').
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite conduct, the rules of acceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Keep dropping opener in jam

indicators.note: dropping the opener removes the first letter

parts.note: preserve is another word for jam

explanation.surface: A jar of jam is kept, though its lid has fallen off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to hold it back, to keep it.

clue.text: Cold, having got left outside? Hot!

indicators.note: the word for left goes around the other letter

parts.note: exited means went out, left

explanation.surface: Someone shivering after being locked out suddenly feels hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot in the sense of worked up or aroused means excited.

clue.text: Compiling, gets agitated about money

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece
something agitated is stirred up, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is worried about cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' mixes GETS into SETG, which goes 'about' TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a crossword means compiling it, a crossword-world synonym.

clue.text: Caught wearing lightweight shoe? Malicious gossip

indicators.note: a foot wearing a shoe is inside it, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a sandal is a light open shoe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A celebrity caught in flimsy shoes becomes the subject of spiteful talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandal is talk that damages reputations, so malicious gossip.

clue.text: Quiet expression of pain knight displayed

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
ow is a cry of pain
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight shows his pain but quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown and displayed are both past participles for put on view.

clue.text: Gold plating finally put on an instrument

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gold plating is finally applied to a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a keyboard musical instrument with pipes.

clue.text: Prior to university, teach about a castle

indicators.note: prior to places the earlier pieces before the next
about signals moving the letters around

explanation.surface: Before going to university, someone teaches about a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the anagram signal for the teach letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Spirit from those ending up on top

indicators.note: the final letter of the word moves up to the top of the down entry

explanation.surface: The prevailing spirit comes from those who rise to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending up on top' moves the last letter of THOSE, E, to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or culture of a group.

clue.text: Try Southern baking

parts.note: baking describes very hot weather

explanation.surface: Have a go at baking in the southern style.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt, as in to have a shot at something.

clue.text: Pole chose to keep side of garden uncared-for

parts.note: N is the north pole

indicators.note: keeping something holds it inside

parts.note: elected means chose

indicators.note: side of a word gives its edge letter, here the first

explanation.surface: A Polish man chose to keep part of his garden, which has been left wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person but means the north pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglected means left without attention, so not cared for.

clue.text: Develop thick hair? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: a thatch is a thick head of hair

explanation.surface: Growing a full head of hair takes a while to start.
explanation.definitionFit: To hatch a plan is to devise and develop it.

clue.text: Delighted prison term's reduced by 50%

indicators.note: cutting a word by half removes its second half

parts.note: a sentence is a prison term

explanation.surface: A prisoner is thrilled that his term has been halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent is slang for thrilled, as in sent into raptures by music.

clue.text: Teenager's party surrounded by beer smell

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed inside the other word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a do is a party
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A youngster's party reeks of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person in their teens, a teenager.
